newsitem.title: USA: Gartner sees 100 mln Internet users by '98.
newsitem.headline: Gartner sees 100 mln Internet users by '98.

text.p: Gartner Group Inc predicts about 100 million people will be using the Internet by the end of 1998, an estimate that Gartner analyst Doug Cayne said may be on the conservative side.
Cayne told a Gartner Group technology symposium here that projecting the number of Internet users is nearly impossible, because of the fast-changing numbers, as more new users log on every day.
"By the year 2000, we expect the Internet to become the dial tone of data communications around the world," Cayne said.
"If I had to pick a single number for now, I'd pick a conservative 30 million users at the start of 1996," Cayne said. There are currently about 250 million PCs in use worldwide, he added.
Cayne also said that high speed access will continue to be a problem for consumers, who will be restrained by data modem speeds until at least 1998.
Gartner, a technology market research firm in Stamford, Conn., predicts that by the year 2001, 50 percent of consumers will still access the Internet and online services via modems.

Another 15 percent will use cable modems, 25 percent will use high-speed digital telephone lines called ISDN, five percent will use hybrid satellite connections and less than five percent will use ADSL, a way to speed up existing telephone lines.
"Getting substantially improved bandwidth (data pipe capacity) is not going to happen," Cayne said. "So if you are designing content, you have to keep this in mind."
